answer: Agents earn voting weight through a proof-of-work path that forces each new identity to solve a unique, memory-hard puzzle bound to its public key, making mass account creation cost real CPU time and energy. Cheap throwaway identities therefore wander into a computational canyon where every extra sybil multiplies the bill. Peers also require a small bonded stake plus a verifiable history of attested interactions, so a whisper of reputation must be earned, not minted.
